group: Real awards from MDHHS's roster, one row per AWARD, in mi_year1_awardees.csv
why: 132 candidates under 'MI - 2026 - RHTP Subrecipients' match a row of the award file on name AND amount, counted as a multiset. RCJ now carries MDHHS's roster ONE ROW PER AWARD. On the 2026-08-27 pull it carried one row per ORGANISATION ('RHTP Subrecipients Award', 14 rows, deflating Michigan by $7,833,333) and RCJ WITHDREW all of those on 2026-09-24. The file was re-extracted in session 64 from MDHHS's 2026-09-24 roster ('as of August 31, 2026'), which ADDED 6 rows ($31,435,045, every one to a Michigan STATE AGENCY as a subrecipient) to the 139-row roster of 2026-09-01; those are rows 140-145 of the file, and the Michigan Veterans Affairs Agency (MVAA) $2,000,000 row is the one RCJ carries. RCJ still lacks 13 of the file's 145 award actions: Berrien County Health Department $150,000; Chippewa County Health Department $150,000; Chippewa-Luce-Mackinac Community Action Agency $350,000; Harbor Beach Community School District School Wellness Program $83,333; Michigan Health Improvement Alliance (MiHIA) $1,500,000; Upper Peninsula Commission for Area Progress (UPCAP) $1,500,000; Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE) Central Michigan $500,000; Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE) Northeast Michigan $500,000; Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity (LEO) - Michigan High Speed Internet Office $9,104,425; Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity (LEO) - Office of Rural Prosperity $16,130,623; Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity (LEO) - Office of Rural Prosperity $600,000; Michigan Department of Education (MDE) - Office of Career and Technical Education $2,099,997; Michigan Department of Education (MDE) - Office of Career and Technical Education $1,500,000. Every row in mi_year1_awardees.csv is built from MDHHS's page, never from RCJ (§0.1).
disqualifying_evidence: name and amount identical to the MDHHS roster row

group: LEO allocations quoted at a rounded or combined figure
why: Real allocations to the Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity (a STATE AGENCY receiving RHTP money as a subrecipient, not the grantor), IN the file since session 64 at MDHHS's own grain, and carried by RCJ at a coarser one (§6.1 mode 4): 'Michigan High-Speed Internet Office' $9,100,000 from 'MI - 2026 - September 2026 RHTP Newsletter'; 'Office of Rural Prosperity' $16,700,000 from 'MI - 2026 - Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Visits Michigan to Explore RHT in Action'. MDHHS's roster prices LEO's High Speed Internet Office at $9,104,425 and its Office of Rural Prosperity at $16,130,623 + $600,000 -- RCJ's Rural Prosperity figure is those rows summed and rounded, so neither RCJ row matches a file row on (name, amount) and neither is counted as in the file. An interagency allocation; never a hospital dollar.

group: State Of Michigan RHTP Budget Narrative line items
why: Genuinely RHTP and one tier too high (§0.2, Oklahoma's defect). These are planning figures out of Michigan's own RHTP Budget Narrative, not award actions. Four of the nine names do later appear on the roster as real awardees AT DIFFERENT AMOUNTS -- Berrien County Health Department is $150,000 in the narrative and holds $150,000 + $100,000 on the roster -- and five appear nowhere on it at all, including 'Northern Michigan Center for Rural Health (Technical Assistance for Hubs)' and 'Thumb Alliance - Sanilac County Health Department', which are project labels rather than the recipient names MDHHS awarded under.
disqualifying_evidence: budget-narrative planning figures, not award actions

group: MDHHS community violence intervention grants -- urban, not RHTP
why: MDHHS's 2026-09-21 release awards '$1.5 million to five organizations' for firearm-violence intervention in Flint, Lansing, Saginaw, Benton Harbor and Detroit, $300,000 each for 2026-09-01 to 2028-09-30. The words 'Rural Health Transformation', 'RHTP' and 'rural' occur ZERO times in it. RCJ files four of the five as Michigan RHTP Tier 3 candidates (§0.1 mode 1, wrong programme) -- the successor to the opioid-settlement release whose eight rows RCJ withdrew on this pull.
disqualifying_evidence: "has awarded $1.5 million to five organizations through a competitive grant process"

group: University of Michigan Injury Prevention Center -- Suicide Prevention Council
why: The Michigan Suicide Prevention Council Report's own funding table: 'The State of Michigan appropriated $125,000 in funding to establish the Michigan Suicide Prevention Council', of which $100,000 is a line, and it thanks the University of Michigan Injury Prevention Center for project management. A state appropriation; RHTP is not mentioned.
disqualifying_evidence: "The State of Michigan appropriated $125,000 in funding"
